Alright, I've been making a series of edits to the index.html to tweak lighting, camera angles, and some object positions. After each edit I try to preview the scene. The preview server started fine, but when I request a screenshot it times out repeatedly. No console warnings or errors are showing up, which suggests the page might not be fully loading or the rendering loop is hanging before any canvas is drawn.

Given that there are no console logs, I need to investigate the state of the page itself. The most straightforward way is to query the DOM from the preview environment. I can use the preview_eval tool to run a small JavaScript expression in the page context. If the document hasn't reached the "complete" readyState, the Three.js initialization code (which likely runs on window load or DOMContentLoaded) might not have executed yet, meaning the canvas element hasn't been created or the renderer hasn't started. Also, checking whether a <canvas> element exists will tell me if the Three.js renderer was able to attach to the DOM.

So the next diagnostic step is to evaluate something like `document.readyState` and also test for the presence of a canvas. Concatenating these into a single string will give a concise result I can read. Therefore I will call the mcp__Claude_Preview__preview_eval tool with the expression `"document.readyState + ' | canvas:' + !!document.querySelector('canvas')"` on the current serverId. This should tell me whether the page is still loading and whether the canvas element exists, helping me pinpoint why the screenshot is timing out.
